ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Fixation of support price of Agricultural Products by States 
*81. SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN: Will the Minister of 
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have taken a decision to auth orize the State 
Governments to fix the support price of Agricultural products which do 
not get the expected price and the lo ss suffered would be shared by the 
State Governments and the Central Government; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government have allotted any amount to any State to 
sustain the loss; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether Government propose to allot any fund to Kerala for 
compensating the loss of Support Price; and 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI AJIT SINGH): (a) to (f) 
A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha. 
Statement 
(a) to (f) No, Sir. The Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) of 25 major 
agricultural commodities are fixed by the Government of India only and 
are uniform throughout the country. The designated central nodal agencies 
are required to intervene in the market and undertake procurement 
operations in case the market prices fall below the MSPs fixed by the 
Government. The losses suffered by the designated central nodal agencies 
in undertaking the procurement operations are reimbursed by the Central 
Government. 
The Government is also implementing Market Intervention Scheme 
1 

RAJYA SABHA       [23 November 2001] 
(MIS) for horticultural commodities and other minor agricultural crops, which are 
perishable in nature. The MIS is implemented for a particular commodity on the 
request of the State Government(s), whicl^are ready to bear 50 per cent of the 
losses, (25% in the case of North-Eastern States), if any, in its implementation. 
No funds are allotted by the Central Government to the State Governments 
under both the schemes of MSP & MIS. 
SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN: Sir, the farming community in our country is 
facing a severe crisis due to the crash in the prices of agricultural products. Even in my 
State, Kerala 29 farmers have already committed suicide during the last three months. 
The prices have gone down considerably . For example, the price of copra was 
Rs. 4y- per kilo and it has come down to Rs. W-; the price of arecanut which was Rs. 
165/- per kilo has come down to Rs. 2W-\ the price of paddy which was Rs. 735/- per 
quintal has come down to Rs. 40(y-; as for black pepper, the price has come down from 
Rs. 240^- to Rs. 67/-; as for ginger, it has come down from Rs. \5/- to Rs. 3.5Q/-; 
in the case of rubber, it has come down from Rs. 69 to Rs. 28. Sir, the support price 
mechanism has been evolved to save the fa rmers from the effect of such a crash in 
prices. But, in most of the cases, the Minimum Support Price evaluation or the 
market intervention is done and the declara tion of the support price is made after 
eight or ; nine months or even one year. During that time, the prices of agricultural 
products, fertilisers, pesticid es and even seeds and the labour cost will go up. In 
almost all the cases, the support  price is not in terms of the reality or in accordance 
with the actual cost of production. So, the inordinate delay is causing much difficulty 
to the farmers in getting the actual pr ice. Also, the procurement takes place 
after the season is over. Part (a) of my supplementary is whether this inordinate delay 
will be rectified by the Government and the support price will be declared in time and 
the products will be procured in time. Part (b) of my supplementary is this. The last 
paragraph of the answer states that no f unds are allotted by the Central Government 
to the State Governments, under both the schemes of MSP and MIS. What is the 
reason for the non-allocation of funds to the States under these two schemes? 
2 

[23 November 2001]       RAJYA SABHA 
SHRI AJIT SINGH: The Minimum Support Prices are fixed by the 
Commission on Agricultural Costs and Prices, and I am not aware that 
they are fixed one year later. Khar iff prices are declared before the 
Khariff procurement begins and the Rabi prices are declared before the 
Rabi crops come into the maiket. So, I do not understand how you are 
saying that the prices are announced on e ye3r later. And these prices are 
determined, based on the cost, based also on the incentives we want to 
give to a certain produce. As far as the allocation of funds is concerned, 
we do not allocate funds to the St ates. The FCI, or whatever the 
procurement agency is, pays the difference between the minimum cost 
and the costs incurred by the States. Under the decentralised scheme of 
procurement, three States are going to procure on their own. Madhya 
Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal are procuring whatever crops are 
there under the MSP, and the FCI pays them the difference. Fund 
allocation is not there to the States, but it does not mean that we do not 
pay. The FCI pays it. The question was whether we allocate any funds. 
SHRI N.K. PREM ACH AND RAN: My second supplementary is this. 
Declaration of the MSP for agricultural produce, without procurement of 
the produce in time, is of no use. The MSP for milling copra has been

copra in time by the procurement agency, i.e., the NAFED. So, 1 want to 
know whether the NAFED will be directed to procure the copra in time so 
as to save the farmers. That is part (a) of my second supplementary. Part 
(b) is this. During the visit of the hon. Prime Minister to Kumarakom in 
Kerala, he offered a package for Kerala in order to save the farmers. And 
a Coconut Technology Mission has been announced by him, and a draft 
proposal, which was submitted by the State Government of Kerala, 
through the Coconut Development Bo ard, has been accepted. But it is 
alleged that it has been revised. Many demands made in the draft proposal 
have been denied. For example, the replacement of the existing diseased 
plants. That scheme has been taken out. I would like to know from the 
hon. Minister as to when

to know whether the proposals submitted by the State Government will be 
taken into account so that the offer of the Coconut Technology Mission,

SHRI AJIT SINGH: Sir, as the hon. Member was saying, NAFED 
procures coconut through the State agencies. Coconut is a year-round 
product. So, NAFED has started the procurement now. In Kerala, we are 
facing some problems because, the High Court has put a ban on it in

Commission has approved the scheme, and it will be implemented through

and we are certainly in touch with the State Government of Kerala. Their 
views and the views of the other coconut-producting States will be taken 
into account. We are discussing this issue with them, we are consulting 
them, and since the Planning Commission, in principle, has approved it, 
we hope it will take effect very soon.

Production of cheaper urea 
*86. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Will the Minister of 
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that imported urea is cheaper than that produced 
in our country; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) what steps Government have taken to make the production of urea 
cheaper in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS 
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI SATYA BRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) to 
(c) The production cost of urea in the country varies from unit to unit 
depending upon the technology, feedstock used, vintage of the plant, 
distance from source of raw materials etc. The production cost of urea in 
the country is higher than the international price, which is primarily on 
account of higher cost of feedstock/ra w materials in India. Urea plants in 
the exporting countries are generally  based on  natural gas.  As per 
available 
26 

[23 November 2001]       RAJYA SABHA 
information, the cost of natural gas in those countries is around US $ 1 
per million BTU or even less, whereas in India the delivered cost of gas is 
around US $ 2.4 per million BTU for the plants based on gas at landfall 
point and about US $ 2.9 for the plants based on gas located on HBJ 
pipeline. The feedstock cost of the plants based on naphtha and fuel 
oil/LSHS is still higher, being in the neighbourhood of US $ 7.7 to 9.2 per 
million BTU and US $ 5.5 to 6.3 per million BTU, respectively. Efforts 
are under way to import Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) for manufacture of 
urea, which is likely to be cheaper than naphtha. However, the cost of 
indigenous urea *may still be higher, due to high transport cost of LNG. 
Pricing of liquid petroleum products viz. naphtha, fuel oil, low sulphur 
heavy stock at import parity price by domestic oil refineries, installation of 
energy saving measures such as purge gas recovery unit etc. and 
promoting technological improvements for improving energy efficiency in urea 
units are some of the measures taken by the units/Government towards 
reducing the cost of production of urea in the country.

remaining 165 out of 567 unauthorised/regularised colonies, 43 out 
of 135 urban villages and 4 out of 44 resettlement colonies and

637. SHRI C. P. THIRUNAVUKKARASU: Will the Minister of 
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have prepar ed a -scheme to simplify and 
rationalise the procedure relating to mode of payment of concessions to 
the fertilizer industry after its de-control; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government have undertaken any cost study of fertilizer 
units to work out concessions; 
(d) if so, the outcome of the study; 
(c) the reaction of Government thereto; and 
(f) the measures suggested by Govern ment to increase efficiency and 
overall performance of the units? 
THE MINISTER . OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS 
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI SATYA BRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) and 
(b) Fresh guidelines laying down the revised procedure for submission of 
bills for payment/recoveries in respect of sales of de-controllcd 
phosphatic & potassic fertilizers under the Concession Scheme for 
decontrolled fertilizers have been issued on 17.5.2001 by the Department 
of Fertilizers. To expedite processing of claims as also to reduce the time 
lag between sales and release of concession, the procedure for certification 
of sales has been rationalised. To achieve these objectives, submission of 
information relating to stocks, production/imports, despatches and closing 
stocks has been de-linked from filing of claim, which is to be submitted 
separately on quarterly basis. Further, in order to put a curb on sale of 
non standard SSP to farmers and need to promote use of specified grades 
of rock phosphate, under the new guidelines a Technical & Audit 
Inspection Cell (TAC) has been constituted to conduct first (1st) time as 
well as six-monthly inspections of SSP manufacturers for ensuring usage of 
specified grades of rock phosph ate from sources notified by the 
Department of Fertilizers from time to time. Some grades of rock 
phosphate along with sources have since been notified by  the  
Department  of Fertilizers.  The  full  text  of the  revised 
89 

RAJYA SABHA        [23 November 2001] 
guidelines is also available on Internet (http^fert.nic.in). Recently, the on 
account payment has also been raised from 80% to 85% and up to 90% 
supported by Bank Guarantee against this 5% payment in respect of 
indigenous manufacturers of phosphatic & potassic (P&K) fertilizers w.e.f. 
1.4.2001. 
(c) to (f) A cost price study in respect of indigenous and imported DAP 
and MOP was undertaken by the Tariff Commission (the erstwhile BICP) 
in the year 1998. Another study of units manufacturing complex grade 
fertilizers has also been undertaken by the Commission. The 
recommendations of the Tariff Commission with minor modifications have 
been implemented w.e.f. 1999-2000 for determination of concession rates 
of phosphatic & potassic fertilizers and the recommendations of the 
Commission in respect of complex fertilizers will form the basis for 
determination of concession rates for these fertilizers under the Concession 
Scheme. As the rates of concession are fixed taking into account the 
efficiency norms for the industry recommended by an independent 
professional body like tariff Commission, they encourage the industry to 
improve efficiency and in turn over-all performance.

ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be pleased to state:

in the Corbett National Park, that the Deputy Ranger was killed and 
some forest guards were injured by the poachers some time in the last 
week of August, 2001;

(c) what are the reasons for the failure  of measures taken so far and 
the security arrangements, to chec k poaching of protected animals in.

BAALU): (a) and (b) Six instances of poaching of elephants between

been beefed up and elaborate combi ng of the forests has been done. In 
one such exercise, Deputy Ranger Shri Bipin Chandra Pandey lost his life 
in an encounter with miscreants on 28th August, 2001 and 3 other forest 
officials were injured. 
(c) Parts and products of elephant, tiger and panther, musk pods, bear 
bile have very lucrative price in the illegal market across our borders and 
in many developed countries. The high pecuniary gains have created a 
large network of organised mafias across the country. The limited staff 
within the forest department and lack of adequate mobility, effective 
communication network, technical skills in intelligence gathering for 
detection of poaching cases and delayed 
104 
 

[23 November 2001]        RAJYA SABHA 
prosecution in courts are major limitations before the forest officials in 
meeting the increasing challenge of poaching and illegal trade,

against hunting and commercial exploitation under the provisions of the 
Wildlife (Protection) act, 1972.

offenders.

672. SHRIMATI VANG A GEETHA : Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the main objectives of Minimum Levels of Learning 
Programme; 
(b) the names of states where Programme has been introduced; and 
(c) the progress made through this programme? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. (S HRIMATI) RITA VERMA): (a) 
Minimum Levels of Learning (MLL) were laid down with the aim that 
irrespective of caste, creed, location or  sex, all children must be given 
education of a comparable standard . The MLL strategy for improving the 
quality of elementary education is an  attempt to combine quality with 
equity. 
(b) As per the submissions in the Satya Pal Anand case in the 
Supreme Court regarding elementary education as a fundamental right 
(1998), 25 States and Union Territories viz. Andhra Pradesh, Assam, 
Bihar, Goa, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya 
Pradesh, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Orissa, Punjab, 
Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Andaman & 
Nicobar Islands, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman & Diu, Delhi and 
Pondicherry have introduced Minimum Levels of Learning (MLL) at 
primary level. 
(c) After the articulation of MLLs, competency-based learning was 
introduced. Development of new text books, training of teachers, 
preparation of work-books, preparation of competency-based books, 
preparation of teachers' manuals, translation of MLL document at primary 
stage in various languages, etc. have been taken up in the. States.

Resources; (v) Student Support and Progression; (vi) Organisation and 
Management; and (vii) Healthy Practices."

Literacy Drive for Women 
†689. SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that presently the illiterate women in the 
country outnumber the men; 
(b) if so, whether Government would propose to introduce any new 
scheme to literate women; and 
(c) if so, by when and if not, in what manner Government propose to 
make women more and more educated? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT [DR. (SHRIMATI) RITA VERMA]: (a) 
According to the 2001 census report (Provisional) the absolute number of 
illiterate women is more than illiterate men, but the following positive 
trends have also emerged:—  
 Reduction in gender gap from 24.84 percentage points in 1991 to 
21.69 percentage points in 2001. 
 Female literacy has increased by 14 .87 percentage points as against 
an increase of 11.72 percentage points in male literacy during 
1991—2001. 
(b) and (c) The following steps taken to improve the female literacy in 
the country: 
1. A scheme of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) has been started for 
Universalization of Elementary Education in a mission mode with district 
as a focus. SSA provides Elementary Education for all children in the age 
group of 6—14 by 2010. The goals are as follows:  
 All children in school, Education Guarantee Scheme center, 
Alternate school, 'Back-to-School' camp by 2003. 
 All children complete five-year primary schooling by 2007. 
 All children complete eight years of schooling by 2010. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

[23 November 2001]        RAJYA SABHA 
 Focus   on   elementary   education   of  satisfactory   quality   with 
emphasis on education for life. 
 Bridge all gender and social category gaps at primary stage by 2007 
and at elementary education level by 2010. 
 Universal retention by 2010. 
Special efforts are being made for improvement of acces s, enrolment, 
retention and achievement of girls in schools under this scheme. 
2. National Literacy Mission (NLM) seeks to attain full literacy, i.e. 
sustainable threshold level of 75 per cent by 2005. It seeks to achieve this 
goal by imparting functional literacy to non-literate in 15—35 year age 
group. Major thrust of the programm e is on promotion of literacy among 
women. In the literacy programmes, 60% of the learners are women and 
around 60% of volunteers also are women and young girls. 
3. Mahila Samakhya Programme seeks to build up capacities, among 
groups of women and contribute towards the empowerment of women in 
rural areas, particularly from socia lly and economically marginalized 
groups.

Economic growth of Railways 
710. SHRI A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of 
RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have taken any steps to stop the sluggish 
economic growth of the Railways; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
166 

[23 November 2001]        RAJYA SABHA 
(c) what steps have been taken by the Railways to attract more freight 
traffic; 
(d) whether Government have stopped all kinds of recruitments due to 
economic crisis; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL): (a) to (c) Rail transportation is basically a 
derived demand, which is entirely dependent upon the core sectors of the 
economy. Due to the general recessi on in the global and the national 
economy, coupled with gradual opening up and liberalization of the core 
sector, the desired level of freight traffic has not materialized. While there 
has been a considerable growth in both railway freight and passenger 
traffic in the past five decades, Railways' share of the freight segment has 
been declining despite best efforts. 
The shortfall in movement of coal, raw material for steel plants, iron 
ore for export, petroleum products and fertilizer is a direct result of a drop 
in the output of these sectors. This is borne out by the negative/declining 
growth rate of infrastructure industries in the first five months of the 
current fiscal. Railways are, however, in a state of preparedness to carry 
any additional traffic that may be of fered by the industry and the core 
sector during the year. 
On the passenger front, it is anticipated that the target of passenger 
earnings envisaged in the Budget will be achieved. 
Following measures have been taken by the Railways to attract freight 
traffic:—  
(i) Domestic Division of Container Corporation of India has been 
activated to pick up piecemeal goods traffic. 
(ii) Powers have been delegated to Zonal Railways to quote special 
lump-sum rate for short lead traffic moving in merry-go-round 
system. 
(iii) Volume Discount Scheme and liberalized station to station rate 
have been notified. 
167 

RAJYA SABHA        [23 November 2001] 
(iv) Participation of private sector for setting up of freight terminals is 
being attempted. A pilot project near Gurgaon has been 
undertaken for this purpose, 
(v) A scheme for running mini rakes has been notified in order to 
cater to demand for less than train load short lead traffic. 
(d) No, Sir. 
(e) Does not arise.

report; and

[23 November 2001]        RAJYA SABHA

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI BACHI SINGH RAWAT): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. 
The Government has studied the news item which appeared in the Indian 
Express of 24th August, 2001. 
The above mentioned news item reiterates the risk of an impending 
earthquake in Himalaya which is also confirmed by independent studies 
commissioned/undertaken by the Department of Science and Technology 
from time to time. It is appropriate to mention that this region falls under 
Zone IV and V (high and very high damage risk zones) of the Seismic 
Zoning Map of India prepared by the Bureau of Indian Standards (IS: 
1893:1984). Zone-V is broadly associated with earthquakes of intensity 
IX and above in the Modified Mercalli Scale ana* Zone IV with intensity 
VIII and above. 
Keeping in view of the vulnerability of this region, the Government 
has got conducted several seismological and other collateral geophysical 
studies for the past two decades to better understand the earthquake 
phenomena and geophysical character of ' various geological faults and 
thrusts zones in the Himalayan region. The seismological observatory 
network in this region has been recently upgraded with state-of-the-art 
instrumentation, data retrieval, processing and analysis. Also, action has 
been initiated to establish a dense network of observatories in a phased 
manner. Besides, to enhance the research capabilities in the field of 
earthquake studies, several research projects have been supported in 
various institutes like: University of Roorkce, Wadia Institute of 
Himalayan Geology, National Geophysical Research Institute and several 
other organizations. 
The inputs of these studies are prov ided to State Governments local 
Governments and other community based organizations to enable them to 
better prepared and aware of the risk s. Bureau of Indian Standards has 
formulated certain codes of building design and construction practice 
which, if strictly followed, will ensure substantial

earthquake. Several steps have also been initiated for public awareness 
through multilingual posters and other methods of information

for earthquake related disasters.

Reviewing Selection Procedure for Sports Awards 
746. SHRI R.P. GOENKA: Will th e Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the criteria laid down for conferring various categories of sports 
awards on sports persons in the country; 
(b) whether Government have reviewed the manner of scrutiny and 
standards laid down for sports awards, like the Arjuna Award, in view of 
the recent controversies and allegations of unfair practices, including 
lobbying in selecting the awardees; 
(c) if so, the details of the review  exercise undertaken, including 
consultations held with leading sports persons/organisations, etc.; and 
(d) the amendments made to rules to make the selection process 
transparent? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI P. RADHAKRISHNAN): (a) A 
Statement is given (Sec below). 
(b) to (d) Yes, Sir. Government is  at present undertaking an exercise 
for reviewing standards laid down for various sports Awards. 
Statement  
The criteria laid down for conferring various categories of sports awards 
on sports persons in the country are as under: 
1   ARJUNA AWARDS 
To be eligible for the Arjuna Award, a person should have had not only 
good performance consistently for the previous three years at the 
National/International level with excellence for the year for which the 
Award is recommended but also should have shown 
204 

[23 November 2001]        RAJYA SABHA 
qualities of leadership, sportsmans hip and sense of discipline. 
Government of India will also consider giving Awards to such sports 
persons who have contributed their life like sports and sports promotion. 
2. SPECIAL AWARDS TO WINNERS IN INTERNATIONAL 
SPORTS EVENTS AND THEIR COACHES 
The special awards are available only for winning medals and titles in 
prestigious international sports events  in the disciplines of sports given 
below, where the competition is fierce and the players enter into the fray 
with burning desire to excels and, ther efore, the medals are hard to come 
by. The other discipline of sports and events have been consciously 
excluded to ensure that really deserving achievements are awarded : 
(i) Olympics,    Asian    Games    and    Commonwealth    Games 
disciplines; 
(ii) Billiards and Snooker; 
(iii) Chess. 
3. RAJIV GANDHI KHEL RATNA AWARDS 
The spectacular and most outstanding performances in the field of 
sports by the sportspersons in a year shall be honoured with the Rajiv 
Gandhi Khel Ratna Award. There will be only one award every year to be 
given either to an individual sportspersons or to more than one person in 
case of team event. If a team is se lected for the Award, all the members 
of the team shall get the Award as envisaged for team events i.e. no 
member of the team will get less than 50% of the award money 
prescribed for. 
4. MAULANA ABUL KALAM AZAD TROPHY 
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Trophy:— This trophy is given annually to 
the University which has given best all-round performance in the year. 
5. DRONACHARYA AWARD 
The award shall be open to coaches whether they work full time or part 
time as coaches, the primary and fundamental emphasis being on 
205 

RAJYA SABHA       [23 November 2001] 
honouring such coaches as have produced outstanding achievement in the 
year for which the award is given and, consistently, very good achievements 
during the three years previous to the year of the award. 
Government of India will also consider giving award to such coaches, 
who have contributed their life time to sports and sports promotion. 
2. The achievement of a coach to be eligble for the award shall be 
judged as follows: 
2 (a) Individual Events 
A coach shall be eligible who produces a sportsperson: 
(i) who wins any medal i.e. gold/silver/bronze in the Olympic 
Games, World Championships, World Cup tournaments for 
Olympic disciplines; or 
(ii) who wins any medal i.e. gold/silver/bronze in the World Cup 
or World Championships in non-Olympic disciplines; or 
(iii) who   creates   a   world   record   which   is   ratified   by   the 
concerned international sports federation; or 
(iv) who wins two gold medals in either Asian Games or the 
Commonwealth Games; or 
(v) who wins three gold medals in Asian Championships or 
Commonwealth Championships. 
A National coach who brings up a contingent of sportspersons which 
gives in individual events a performance better than that compared to the 
previous best as judged by the tally of medals (gold and total) won 
whether in the Olympics Games, World Championships, Commonwealth 
Games, Commonwealth Championships, Asian Games and Asian 
Championships. 
2 (b) Team Events 
A coach shall be eligible if he is responsible for training teams which 
win: 
206 

[23 November 2001]        RAJYA SABHA 
(i) Any medal; gold, silver or bronze in the Olympic Games, 
World Cup or World Championships in Olympic or non-
Olympic disciplines, provided that the performance is either 
better or equal to the best performance achieved earlier; or 
(ii) 2 gold medals—one in Asian Games and another in Asian 
Championships held earlier or later; or 
(Hi) 2 gold  medals—one  in  Asian  Games  and  the  other  in 
Commonwealth Games held either earlier or later. 
2 (c) Indigenous Sports 
A coach who is responsible for outstanding improvement in the 
performance of individuals or a team as compared with such performance 
in the previous three years and th rough whose coaching a team obtains 
winning position, shall also be eligible for the award.
